# Printable Substrate with Enhanced Print Quality and Mechanical Properties

This article describes a specialized printable substrate engineered to deliver superior print performance while maintaining the structural integrity necessary for practical applications. The substrate is characterized by a showthrough value of approximately 0.14 or less, coupled with an opacity value of at least 88%. This combination of properties is critical for ensuring minimal print bleed-through from one side of the sheet to the other, while simultaneously providing the high print clarity and contrast that end users expect from quality printed materials.

## Base Composition

At the core of this printable substrate is a paper base constructed from paper fibers, engineered with a basis weight ranging from approximately 12 to 32 lbs per 1300 square feet. This basis weight range allows the substrate to remain lightweight and cost-effective while still providing an adequate structural foundation to support subsequent processing and printing operations.

To further tailor the properties of the substrate, a substrate filler may be incorporated into the paper base in an amount ranging from 0 to approximately 30% by weight of the paper substrate. The inclusion of this filler—whether at minimal or more substantial concentrations—provides manufacturers with the flexibility to fine-tune the composition of the substrate, optimizing characteristics such as opacity, brightness, and printability according to specific application requirements.

## Surface Treatment for Print Performance

A key feature of this substrate is the application of a surface size layer, which plays an essential role in achieving the desired print quality outcomes. This layer contains up to approximately 50 lbs per ton of a starch-based surface sizing agent, combined with a multivalent metal salt drying agent. The synergistic action of these components significantly enhances the substrate's interaction with printing inks.

Specifically, this surface size formulation enables the substrate to achieve a black print density of at least 0.8 when used with pigmented inks, ensuring bold, sharp, and visually striking printed images. Additionally, when dye-based inks are employed, the substrate demonstrates a waterfastness of at least 85%, indicating strong resistance to smearing or fading upon exposure to moisture—a critical performance attribute for documents and images that may encounter incidental water contact.

## Mechanical Strength Characteristics

Beyond its print quality attributes, the printable substrate exhibits robust mechanical properties essential for handling, processing, and end-use durability. The substrate demonstrates a machine direction (MD) tensile strength of at least approximately 12 lbs per inch, reflecting strong resistance to tearing or breaking along the direction of manufacture. Complementing this, the substrate also achieves a cross direction (CD) tensile strength of at least approximately 6 lbs per inch, ensuring adequate strength perpendicular to the machine direction as well.

## Method of Preparation

In addition to detailing the composition and performance characteristics of the substrate, the article also outlines a comprehensive method for its preparation. This method encompasses the selection and formulation of paper fibers, the incorporation of substrate fillers at appropriate concentrations, and the application of the surface size layer under controlled conditions to achieve the specified sizing agent and drying agent levels. Through this carefully designed process, the resulting printable substrate successfully balances lightweight construction, tunable composition, excellent print quality, and reliable mechanical performance—making it well-suited for a variety of printing applications where both aesthetic and functional demands must be met.

# Printable Paper Substrate with Low Showthrough and High Opacity

## Background of the Invention

In the field of printing media, particularly for inkjet printing applications, there exists a persistent challenge in producing paper substrates that simultaneously achieve high print quality, minimal showthrough, and adequate opacity while maintaining acceptable strength characteristics. Showthrough—the visibility of printed images from the reverse side of a sheet—becomes especially problematic when printing double-sided documents or when using aqueous inkjet inks that tend to penetrate deeply into paper fibers. Similarly, opacity, which relates to a sheet's ability to prevent light transmission, is critical for ensuring that printed content on one side does not interfere with the readability of content on the opposite side.

Conventional paper substrates often fail to address these issues adequately, particularly when subjected to the demands of modern inkjet printing technology, which requires precise control over ink absorption, drying time, and pigment or dye fixation. Existing solutions frequently involve trade-offs: increasing basis weight to improve opacity can raise production costs and reduce sheet flexibility, while surface treatments designed to reduce showthrough may compromise print density or waterfastness. There remains a need in the art for an improved paper substrate construction that resolves these competing demands through a carefully balanced combination of base sheet composition and surface treatment chemistry.

## Summary of the Invention

The present invention provides a printable paper substrate specifically engineered to deliver low showthrough and high opacity while maintaining excellent print quality metrics suitable for both pigmented and dye-based inkjet inks. The substrate comprises a base sheet formed from paper fibers having a specified basis weight, optionally incorporating a filler material to enhance opacity and other physical properties. This base sheet is further treated with a surface size layer that includes a starch-based sizing agent in combination with a multivalent metal salt acting as a drying agent.

The paper fibers utilized in the base sheet may be derived from a variety of pulping processes, including chemical, mechanical, or combination pulps, and are selected and processed to achieve a basis weight that supports the desired balance of opacity, strength, and printability. The optional filler component, which may include materials such as calcium carbonate, clay, titanium dioxide, or other conventional papermaking fillers, is incorporated in an amount effective to further increase the opacity of the substrate without unduly compromising its strength or surface characteristics.

The surface size layer, applied to one or both sides of the base sheet, plays a critical role in controlling ink absorption and setting behavior. The starch sizing agent within this layer serves multiple functions, including improving the surface strength of the paper, reducing fiber raising during printing, and contributing to the reduction of showthrough by limiting excessive ink penetration into the sheet structure. The multivalent metal salt, functioning as a drying agent, interacts with the ink components—particularly with dye-based and pigmented inks—to promote rapid fixation at the surface of the substrate. This interaction is particularly beneficial in enhancing waterfastness for dye-based inks and improving print density for pigmented inks, as the multivalent metal ions can react with anionic components of the ink to precipitate or immobilize colorants near the sheet surface rather than allowing them to wick further into the paper structure.

## Detailed Description of Preferred Embodiments

In accordance with the invention, the base sheet is formed using conventional papermaking techniques, including wet-end fiber furnish preparation, forming, pressing, and drying operations. The basis weight of the paper fibers is selected to fall within a range that provides sufficient bulk and opacity while remaining compatible with high-speed printing equipment and typical paper handling requirements. Those skilled in the art will recognize that basis weight can be adjusted depending on the intended end-use application, whether for standard office printing, photographic-quality reproduction, or other specialized inkjet printing needs.

The optional filler, when included, is incorporated into the fiber furnish prior to sheet formation or may be applied as part of a filled surface treatment. The selection and loading level of filler material is coordinated with the fiber composition and basis weight to achieve the target opacity value without introducing excessive dusting, linting, or reduction in sheet strength.

Following formation of the base sheet, a surface sizing operation is performed to apply the size composition containing the starch sizing agent and multivalent metal salt drying agent. This surface treatment may be applied using conventional size press equipment, including but not limited to puddle size presses, metered size presses, or other coating application methods known in the papermaking art. The starch sizing agent may include native or modified starches, such as oxidized starch, enzyme-converted starch, or cationic starch derivatives, selected based on compatibility with the metal salt component and the desired viscosity and film-forming properties of the size solution.

The multivalent metal salt drying agent is selected from compounds capable of providing polyvalent cations, such as calcium, magnesium, aluminum, or zinc salts, which interact favorably with ink components to promote rapid drying and fixation. The concentration of the metal salt within the surface size formulation is controlled to achieve the desired balance between print quality enhancement and processability of the size solution during application.

## Performance Characteristics

The resulting paper substrate, prepared according to the methods described herein, exhibits a combination of performance characteristics that render it particularly well-suited for high-quality inkjet printing applications. Specifically, the substrate achieves a showthrough value of about 0.14 or less, as measured using standard optical density testing methods, indicating minimal visibility of printed content from the reverse side of the sheet. This low showthrough value is particularly advantageous for duplex printing applications and for documents where print quality on both sides of the sheet is essential.

The substrate further exhibits an opacity of at least 88%, ensuring that the sheet provides adequate light-blocking properties even at relatively low basis weights. This high opacity value contributes to the overall print quality and professional appearance of printed documents, particularly when printing text or images that require sharp contrast and minimal interference from the reverse side.

With respect to print quality, the substrate achieves a black print density of at least 0.8 when printed with pigmented inkjet inks, indicating strong, dark, and well-defined printed images. This print density value is indicative of good ink holdout and proper interaction between the pigmented ink components and the surface size layer, resulting in vibrant and legible printed output.

For dye-based inkjet inks, the substrate demonstrates a waterfastness value of at least 85%, reflecting the effectiveness of the multivalent metal salt drying agent in fixing dye colorants at the sheet surface and reducing their susceptibility to smearing, running, or fading upon exposure to moisture. This waterfastness characteristic is particularly important for documents that may be subjected to humid conditions or incidental contact with water.

Additionally, the paper substrate is characterized by specified machine direction (MD) and cross direction (CD) tensile strength values, ensuring that the sheet maintains adequate mechanical integrity for handling, feeding through printing equipment, and general use. These tensile strength specifications are achieved through appropriate selection of fiber furnish composition, refining conditions, and surface treatment application, ensuring that the enhanced printing performance characteristics do not come at the expense of overall sheet durability.

## Method of Preparation

The method for preparing the printable paper substrate of the present invention generally comprises the steps of forming a base sheet from paper fibers having the specified basis weight, optionally incorporating a filler material into the fiber furnish or applying it as part of a surface treatment, and subsequently applying a surface size composition comprising a starch sizing agent and a multivalent metal salt drying agent to at least one surface of the base sheet.

The base sheet formation step may be carried out using conventional Fourdrinier, twin-wire, or other paper machine configurations known in the art, with process parameters adjusted to achieve the target basis weight and physical properties. Following sheet formation and initial drying, the surface size composition is prepared by combining the starch sizing agent with the multivalent metal salt drying agent in an aqueous solution, with concentrations and ratios selected to achieve the desired performance characteristics upon application.

The surface size composition is then applied to the base sheet using conventional size press or coating equipment, followed by drying to remove excess moisture and set the surface treatment layer. The resulting substrate may be subjected to additional finishing operations, such as calendering, to achieve desired surface smoothness and caliper characteristics, provided that such operations do not adversely affect the opacity, showthrough, print density, waterfastness, or tensile strength properties specified for the substrate.

## Advantages of the Invention

The printable paper substrate of the present invention offers several advantages over conventional paper products used for inkjet printing applications. By combining a carefully selected base sheet composition with a surface size treatment incorporating both a starch sizing agent and a multivalent metal salt drying agent, the invention achieves a synergistic improvement in print quality metrics that would be difficult to attain through either component alone. The resulting substrate provides excellent opacity and reduced showthrough, enabling high-quality duplex printing, while simultaneously delivering strong print density with pigmented inks and superior waterfastness with dye-based inks. These performance characteristics, combined with appropriate tensile strength properties, render the substrate suitable for a wide range of high-quality printing applications, including business documents, marketing materials, and photographic reproductions, where both print quality and paper durability are of paramount importance.

# The Word "Also"

"Also" is one of those small but essential words that we use constantly without giving it much thought. As an adverb, it serves to add information, connect ideas, or indicate that something applies in addition to what has already been stated.

## Function in Language

The primary purpose of "also" is to signal addition. When we say "I like coffee. I also like tea," we're telling the listener that the second statement builds upon or extends the first. It creates a sense of continuity and helps organize thoughts in a logical sequence.

"Also" can appear in different positions within a sentence:

- **At the beginning**: "Also, don't forget to bring your umbrella."
- **In the middle**: "She also enjoys hiking on weekends."
- **Near the end**: "He wanted to come along also."

## Synonyms and Alternatives

Depending on context, "also" can often be replaced with words like:
- Additionally
- Furthermore
- Moreover
- As well
- Too
- In addition

Each of these carries slightly different connotations. "Furthermore" and "moreover" tend to feel more formal, often used in academic or professional writing, while "also" and "too" fit naturally into everyday conversation.

## Why Small Words Matter

Words like "also" might seem insignificant compared to nouns and verbs that carry the main content of a sentence. However, these connecting words play a crucial role in making language flow smoothly and helping ideas relate to one another. Without them, our speech and writing would sound choppy and disconnected, forcing listeners or readers to work harder to understand how different pieces of information fit together.

In essence, "also" exemplifies how even the simplest words carry important structural weight in communication, guiding meaning and helping us build coherent, connected thoughts.

# ABSTRACT

**PRINTABLE PAPER PRODUCT WITH ENGINEERED SURFACE SIZING AND METAL SALT DRYING AGENTS FOR DUAL-CHEMISTRY INKJET PERFORMANCE**

A printable paper substrate is disclosed comprising a cellulosic base sheet having a basis weight of between about 60 to 120 g/m², treated with a surface sizing composition and a metal salt-based drying agent formulated to optimize print quality, dry time, and durability for both pigment-based and dye-based inkjet inks.

The surface sizing agent comprises a blend of oxidized starch or polyvinyl alcohol (PVA), present at 0.5 to 3.0 g/m² dry coat weight, in combination with an alkyl ketene dimer (AKD) or alkenyl succinic anhydride (ASA) internal size, to achieve a Cobb60 water absorptiveness value of 20 to 35 g/m², thereby balancing ink holdout with controlled fluid penetration. The surface size layer further incorporates a cationic fixing agent, such as a polyamine-epichlorohydrin resin or polydiallyldimethylammonium chloride (polyDADMAC), applied at 0.1 to 1.5 wt% based on total coating solids, to promote rapid immobilization of anionic dye molecules and pigment particles upon contact with the paper surface.

A metal salt drying agent, selected from calcium chloride, magnesium chloride, aluminum sulfate, or polyaluminum chloride, is incorporated into the surface treatment at a concentration of 0.2 to 2.0 wt% (dry basis), functioning to accelerate ink vehicle absorption, reduce coalescence and feathering, and promote rapid fixation of colorants through ionic interaction with anionic dye chromophores and pigment dispersant systems. The metal salt agent further imparts hygroscopic moisture regulation, contributing to reduced curl and enhanced dimensional stability under variable humidity conditions (30–80% RH).

The resulting paper product exhibits the following performance characteristics: for pigment-based inkjet inks, an optical density (OD) of ≥1.35 for black and ≥1.10 for process colors, dry time of ≤3 seconds, and smudge resistance rated ≥4 on a 5-point scale; for dye-based inkjet inks, an OD of ≥1.40 for black and ≥1.15 for process colors, dry time of ≤5 seconds, water-fastness rating of ≥3 on a 5-point scale, and edge acuity (print sharpness) of ≥85% coverage uniformity with minimal wicking (<150 µm bleed radius). The paper further demonstrates a gloss differential of less than 10 GU between printed and unprinted regions, and a light-fastness rating of ≥6 on the Blue Wool Scale after 72 hours of accelerated UV exposure.

This paper product is suitable for high-speed inkjet printing applications, including photographic reproduction, document printing, and commercial graphics, wherein compatibility with both aqueous pigment and dye-based ink formulations is required without substantial reformulation of the printing substrate or ink chemistry.
